new_statements.quote: [p.73, sec. 3.4.8] Stress is usually not indicated, since it regularly falls on the penultimate syllable in all Tomini-Tolitoli languages. Only the exceptions to this rule are marked. Primary stress is marked by an acute accent <´>, secondary stress (i.e. lengthening of reduplicated syllables) by a grave accent (`). [p.72, sec. 3.4.7] ... they do not cause stress to move to the penultimate syllable (i.e. words with a paragogic vowel are stressed on the ante-penultima ...) ... In Tialo, paragogic vowels seem to occur very regularly at the end of every consonant-final (phonological) word. [p.10] dalam bahasa Tialo kata 'ungkul 'kulit' biasanya diucapkan sebagai ['úŋkule]. Perlu dicatat bahwa penambahan bunyi vokal tidak merubah pola dasar penekanan: penekanan tetap pada suku kata kedua dari akhir pada sebuah akar kata.
new_statements.translation: p.10 (Indonesian): 'in Tialo the word 'ungkul 'skin' is usually pronounced ['uŋkule]. Note that the addition of the vowel does not change the basic stress pattern: stress stays on the second syllable from the end of the root.' (Preceding sentence on the same page: 'Stress in the Tomini-Tolitoli languages regularly falls on the second syllable from the end, e.g. Dampelas polu 'stone' is pronounced [pólu] not [polú] ...')

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word in Tialo (as in all Tomini-Tolitoli languages); suffixes shift stress rightward to keep it penultimate, whereas the paragogic vowel E (near-obligatory in Tialo after word-final consonants) and enclitics/free possessor forms do not count, so consonant-final words in isolation surface with antepenultimate stress (['uŋkule] = 'ungkul + E).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Only 'secondary stress' mentioned is the lengthening/prominence of the reduplicant in accented CV-reduplication (RDP1), marked with a grave accent in the word lists (sec. 3.4.8, 3.5.10); no rhythmic secondary stress described.
new_statements.exceptions: Exceptions marked with acute accent in the word lists: (a) word-final shortened long vowels bear final stress (mainly southern Tomini languages, e.g. Balaesang); (b) stress may fall on the first member of a sequence of unlike vowels (táipang ~ taípang 'mango'; Indonesian intro: VVKV sequences often stress the first vowel); (c) paragogic E does not attract stress (surface antepenult); (d) Balaesang-only final closed-syllable stress. Suffix vs clitic: suffixed forms get regular penultimate stress, clitics/free forms do not shift stress (p.91-92; Tialo has enclitic possessor forms, e.g. labang E mami).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word (Himmelmann 1991:51 'falls on the penultimate syllable of a (phonological) word and remains penultimate when suffixes or clitics are added'); data are elicited citation forms/word lists tape-recorded in the field (Tialo lists from Lambunu, Ongka etc.). Note Himmelmann 2018 later reanalyses areal 'penultimate stress' in Totoli as phrase-final edge tones, but no such reanalysis has been published for Tialo.
new_statements.identity_note: The language Glottolog/Ethnologue call 'Tomini' (tomi1243, txm) is the one Himmelmann calls 'Tialo (Tomini)' (NUSA 33 p.49; PL-511 pp.15, 19; Glottolog alt names Tialo, Tiadje, Mouton). Himmelmann's stress statement is framed for 'all Tomini-Tolitoli languages' on the basis of his own fieldwork word lists (>=1200 items per language, Tialo included, with Tialo examples throughout); the Tialo-specific sentences concern the paragogic vowel (very regular in Tialo) which does not attract stress. Not a dialect issue: Tialo and Dondo (dond1249) are described as very similar/mutually intelligible but treated as separate languages.

sources.citation: Himmelmann, Nikolaus P. 1991. Tomini-Tolitoli sound structures. NUSA 33: 49-70.
sources.note: Sample p.49 includes 'Tialo (Tomini)'. Sec. 2.1 Stress p.51: 'Stress placement is very regular in Tomini-Tolitoli languages... It falls on the penultimate syllable of a (phonological) word and remains penultimate when suffixes or clitics are added' (bati / ba'tinye). Sec. 2.2: paragogic /e/ leaves stress on the antepenult (Lauje examples); p.64 notes the paragogic vowel was common in isolated words from Tialo speakers. Detailed treatment is of Lauje and Totoli, not Tialo.
